startup.context: Compose build and detached start succeeded. Verified the app responded with HTTP 200 at /rest/admin/application-version and the container reported healthy.

scanPrep.context:
Summary: Rebuilt the patched Juice Shop service and verified that login, reset-password, 2FA, and CAPTCHA-related anti-automation controls are relaxed enough for DAST without triggering rate limits.
Change: Rebuilt and recreated only the `juice-shop` service with `docker compose -f docker-compose.dast.yml up -d --build juice-shop` so the existing source-level relaxations took effect in the running app.
Change: Confirmed the code-level anti-automation relaxations now active in the rebuilt app: `server.ts` keeps the discovered `express-rate-limit` protections on `/rest/user/reset-password`, `/rest/2fa/verify`, `/rest/2fa/setup`, and `/rest/2fa/disable` at `max: 999999`, and `routes/captcha.ts` / `routes/imageCaptcha.ts` leave server-side CAPTCHA checks as pass-through middleware (`next()`).
Change: Queried runtime-exposed settings from the running app (`/rest/admin/application-configuration`) and container runtime env (`docker inspect`); no additional runtime-configured rate/throttle/captcha controls were exposed beyond the source-registered middleware already patched.
Change: Verified post-rebuild behavior with rapid POSTs against real processing endpoints: 6 successful login POSTs to `/rest/user/login` using `admin@juice-sh.op` / `admin123` all returned HTTP 200, 5 rapid POSTs to `/rest/user/reset-password` all returned the underlying business-logic 401 without any 429/throttle text, and 5 rapid POSTs to `/rest/2fa/verify` all returned HTTP 401 without rate-limit responses.
Recovery guidance (security controls): If a future prep pass needs to re-apply or confirm this state, inspect `server.ts`, `routes/captcha.ts`, and `routes/imageCaptcha.ts`, then rebuild only the app service with an example like `docker compose -f docker-compose.dast.yml up -d --build juice-shop`. After the container is healthy, verify with repeated POSTs to `/rest/user/login` using a known valid account (for example `admin@juice-sh.op` / `admin123`) and also hit discovered guarded endpoints such as `/rest/user/reset-password` and `/rest/2fa/verify` several times, checking for any HTTP 429 or response text mentioning throttling/rate limiting. The runtime config endpoint `/rest/admin/application-configuration` is useful for checking whether new runtime-exposed settings appear in later versions.
Recovery guidance (2FA/MFA): 2FA exists in this app via routes/2fa.ts and login enforcement in routes/login.ts when Users.totpSecret is non-empty. For future scan prep, verify with code search and DB checks such as: inspect data/static/users.yml and routes/login.ts; query SQLite inside the app container with docker exec juice-shop-juice-shop-1 /nodejs/bin/node -e "const sqlite3=require('sqlite3'); const db=new sqlite3.Database('/juice-shop/data/juiceshop.sqlite'); db.all(\"SELECT id,email,role,isActive,totpSecret FROM Users WHERE email='bright@test.com'\", (_,r)=>console.log(r))"; and confirm login plus protected access by POSTing to /rest/user/login and then calling /rest/user/authentication-details with the returned Bearer token. If 2FA ever blocks the scan user, clear it with an update like setting totpSecret='' for that user and then restart only the juice-shop service with the verified compose file if needed.
